# User interface: documented functions (`ui`)

Reference table generated in the documentation round of 2026-10-31 and extended in the rounds of 2026-11-04. Each row is a function that reached the `documented` stage (`docs/PROGRESS.md`): its prototype, purpose, return value, side effects and callers, read from the Ghidra decompilation with the names of that round. The same text is the function's plate comment in Ghidra (`re/documented*.tsv`, applied by `tools/ghidra/ApplySignatures.java`). How the subsystem works as a whole is in [`../ui.md`](../ui.md); pointers to structures are typed `void *` and the structure is named in the summary.

Functions: 2332 (BOOT.BIN 195, rel_deck 276, rel_duel_draw 853, rel_duel_mgr 139, rel_field 224, rel_title 645).

## `rel_duel_mgr`

| Address | Prototype | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x08e9e5a0` | `void ui_duel_start_open(void)` | Opens the duel start (rock-paper-scissors) screen: starts loading its archive with ui_duel_start_load_archive, waits frame by frame (thunk_system_wait_frame) until the load-done flag 0x08eba1d4 is set, then initialises the screen with ui_duel_start_init([0x08eba1d8] archive buffer, [0x08ebaa58] heap). Side effects: those of the callees (archive load, work area allocation). Callers: 1 (system_duel_mgr_scene_main). |
| `0x08e9e5f8` | `int ui_duel_start_run_loop(void)` | Frame loop of the duel start screen: clears 0x08eba1f0, then each frame runs ui_duel_start_update; whenever it returns a positive value, stores value - 1 (the turn-order choice, 0 = first) in the duel setup buffer +0x18c, flipped (xor 1) in a link duel when the local duel side (thunk_system_net_api_get_local_duel_side) is 1. Until the duel modules are loaded it steps system_duel_mgr_step_module_loading and, when that reports completion, marks the work area ready (ui_duel_start_set_modules_ready). Clears 0x08eba1dc each frame and waits a frame. Returns 1 once the modules are loaded and the update returns more than 2 (screen freed), or 0 when 0x08eba1dc is 0 and system_duel_mgr_is_link_lost reports a lost link. Side effects: setup buffer +0x18c, 0x08eba1f0, 0x08eba1dc, module loading. Callers: 1 (system_duel_mgr_scene_main). |
| `0x08e9e954` | `bool ui_duel_result_run_loop(void)` | Frame loop of the duel result screen: while the abort word 0x08eba030 is 0 and the result screen state 0x08eba03c is 7, runs ui_duel_result_update and waits a frame with system_duel_mgr_wait_frame_check_link. On update result 2 (rematch, hypothesis medium) clears the words +0x20..+0x2c and halfwords +0x34..+0x3a of the duel setup tail block and restores the 0x858-byte duel setup copy 0x08eba1fc into the setup buffer (memcpy), returning true; on result 1 returns true when thunk_duel_core_get_match_result is 0. Returns false when the loop is left through 0x08eba030 or a state other than 7. Side effects: the duel setup buffer and tail block. Callers: 1 (system_duel_mgr_scene_main). |
| `0x08e9edb4` | `void ui_duel_start_init(void *archive, void *heap)` | Allocates and clears the 0xe8-byte duel start work area from heap into 0x08ebaa90 (heap kept at +0xc0, archive at +0xcc after container_ehp_bind_with_callback(0, archive)). Selects the mode in bits 0-1 of word +0: 0 = full rock-paper-scissors; in a tag duel (setup +0x191 == 2) with a non-zero count u16 at tail block +0x34, the entry u16 tail[+0x34 + 2*count] gives 2 -> mode 1 with byte +3 bit0 = 1 (player picks the turn order), 1 -> mode 1 with bit0 = 0, 3 -> mode 0; setup +0x190 == 5 or 6 -> mode 2 (versus screen only). In a link duel stores the local peer index (bits 0-3), local duel side (bits 4-5) and a bit6 'local peer is its side's peer' in byte +0xc4. Enables font shadow and colour codes, sets the font language flags (Japanese: flag_1 on, trim-wrap off; other languages the reverse), sets state 1 (word +0 = 4), starts a 0x10-frame black fade-in, hides the loading overlay and, unless it is a tag duel with a non-zero tail +0x34, plays BGM track 9 (setup +0x194 == 4 or 5) or 8. No return value. Side effects: 0x08ebaa90 and the work area, font flags, fade, loading overlay, BGM. Callers: 1 (ui_duel_start_open). |
| `0x08e9f14c` | `int ui_duel_start_update(void)` | State machine of the duel start screen, state = bits 2-9 of word +0 of the work area 0x08ebaa90: 1 waits for the fade-in, then in mode 2 creates the versus screen (ui_duel_versus_create kind 8, or 9 when setup +0x192 == 2) and enters state 0xb, else plays the intro (ui_duel_start_play_member2_anim(0), sound 0x7a7c) and enters 2; 2 when the intro ends creates the versus banner (kind 10), plays member2 clip 1 and goes to state 8 (mode 1), 5 (hands laid out with ui_janken_init_hand_layout) or, in a link duel, to 4 (tag duel with tail +0x34, data exchange) or 3 (after link packet (4,1)); 3 waits for the link sync then ui_janken_reset_round; 4 exchanges a 0x100-byte block of the setup buffer through a 0x400-byte heap buffer (system_net_api_set_block_transfer / exchange_data_blocks), copies 0xc0 bytes per player record (setup +0x230 + i*0x1ac) for characters of category 5, then resets the round and sets byte +0xc5 bit1; 5 tweens both hand rows in (ui_janken_step_hand_tween(0x18, side)), shows the cursor, sets the prompt (strTbl index 2 or 4) and enters 6; 6 ui_janken_update_choice; 7 ui_janken_update_reveal; 8 plays the turn-order clip, picks a random first/second (byte +6 bits 5-6) when the opponent decides, sets the prompt (index 3, 4 or 5) and enters 9; 9 ui_janken_update_link_exchange; 10 returns ui_janken_update_result; 0xb returns ui_duel_start_update_versus; 0xc waits for the fade then enters 0xd, returning 1 (go first, byte +6 bits 3-4 == 0) or 2; 0xd frees the versus screen and the work area and returns 3.
